Subject: Post-demo SLO + customer-led load test: next steps & IP allowlist

Hi Liam —

Great to chat earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get your customer-led load test scheduled and staffed: 

1) SLO targets we agreed (for reference):
   - 95th latency <= 220ms for text-gen (512 token avg)
   - P99 tail <= 1.2s for streaming responses
   - Sustained throughput target: 350 requests/minute across 10 concurrent sessions

2) Test artifacts I can provide today:
   - k6 script bundle with two profiles (burst and steady-state) — attachment: northwind-k6-scripts-v2.tar.gz
   - SLO matrix in Excel: SLO-matrix-northwind.xlsx
   - IP allowlist template (CSV) for your infra team to paste into firewall rules

3) What we need from you to proceed:
   - Confirm your test window (we suggested Tue 2026-06-23 09:00–12:00 PT as a tentative slot)
   - Provide IP ranges to add to Redwood allowlist (or we can give static egress IPs if you prefer)
   - Create a test account/service key for the run (we prefer a scoped key limited to the test model)

4) Roles on Redwood side: 
   - Ben Carter (SE) will own script tuning and live run support
   - Marcus Lin (SRE) will monitor GPU pools, routing and fallback policies during the window

Schedule suggestion: do a 30-minute pre-flight on the Monday before the run to validate access, then run a 2-hour stress window with a 15-minute canary.

If that looks good, reply with the preferred test window and the contact for your infra person so we can exchange the IP allowlist CSV.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Forwarding Liam's confirmation. Notes for the run prep: 

- Marcus: please pre-provision a small canary deployment (2 GPUs) pinned to the quantized variant we'll use for the test. If we see tails > P99 target during canary, we'll switch to the float-16 variant for the steady-state run.
- I'll review the k6 scripts Liam mentioned. From the quick look: their steady-state profile opens 10 concurrent VUs per operator session, which would mean 80 VUs aggregated — we should validate session multiplexing behavior so we don't double-count concurrency.
- Ops: I'll prepare a short runbook for the Monday pre-flight with exact API key placement and log collection steps (we want token-level latency traces and per-model token counts).

Marcus — can you confirm the GPU pool is available Tuesday morning for a 3-hour window (8–11 PT on our side to allow a pre-warm)? Also confirm whether IP allowlisting will be manual or automated in our firewall.

Thanks,
Ben
